AnchorPoints Farms of the Future

A Future Rooted in Good Ground • Okmulgee, Oklahoma

Why this land matters to all of us

This is a community project, and it starts with the ground beneath it. AnchorPoints Farms of the Future is planned as a state-of-the-art aquaponics farm and training and education center, designed to be ADA-compliant, AI-automated, solar-powered, energy-efficient, and climate-controlled: a place for fresh, locally grown food, hands-on education, workforce training, and opportunities for young people, families, and neighbors.

Our family-owned land still carries a loan balance of $177,648.80, and that debt is slowing land preparation and delaying construction of the training facility. Every gift goes first toward paying down the land loan so the property can be debt-free before any building begins. Lenders have informed us that we can't take on additional financing at this time, until the land is paid off, which is why we're asking our family, friends and communities for help with this first step. If more is raised beyond that, the extra will go toward land development and the facility.

Our campaign goal starts at $9,000 and will grow in stages up to $190,000. That covers the $177,648.80 balance plus payment-processing fees (2.9% + $0.30 per donation), so the full balance can be paid off. We are not a nonprofit organization, and gifts are not tax-deductible.

The pictures below show the land today and the vision it is growing toward. Each gift brings that vision a little closer for everyone it will serve.

Meet the Family Behind AnchorPoints

AnchorPoints Farms of the Future is a minority-owned, family-owned project, owned by Leon White and his four daughters. It is built for something bigger than one family: the future of our children, teens, young adults, and under-served neighbors in Okmulgee and the communities around us.

Leon brings training, education, and hands-on aquaponics experience. Daily operations and educational training are planned to be run by a team of seasoned professionals, described below.

Our Professional Expert Team

The family owns the land. Daily operations and educational training are planned to be led by experienced professionals in agriculture, aquaponics, infrastructure, and youth education.

Technical Advisor & Aquaponics Systems Designer

Our technical advisor is also our site planner, site developer, and mentor, and he is partnering with us on this community project. He has 18+ years designing, building, and operating aquaponics and RAS (recirculating aquaculture) systems, has owned and operated his own aquaponics business for 12 years (which he continues to run), and co-developed commercial RAS and hydroponic systems. He has installed systems for schools, tribes, and commercial farms.

He guides our system design, facility development, water-quality and biosecurity practices, production planning, and workforce training. He also holds business and economics degrees, including an M.B.A.

Horticulture Expert & ADA Compliance Advisor

A retired infrastructure and building engineer with 15 years of horticulture experience supporting our plant production. He also advises on ADA-compliant design and on following building rules and guidelines. Construction will be carried out by licensed Oklahoma builders.

Youth & Community Garden Consultant

A 12-year veteran of community gardens and plant production, guiding our youth and community programs.

Aquaponics Technician

A college-trained aquaponics technician supporting day-to-day system care.

Production, Food Processing & Delivery

A team member experienced in production services and food processing, who will also help get fresh food to our community.

Team members are not named here to respect their privacy.

Learning, Opportunity & Growth for Everyone

Once the land is secured, AnchorPoints is planned as an education and community center, not just a farm. We are also eager to partner with colleges and offer internships to their students. Here is what we hope to offer.

Youth

Hands-on, real-world learning that makes science and agriculture exciting.

  • Aquaponics and STEM education
  • Youth agricultural leadership programs
  • Mentoring and confidence-building
  • Outdoor classrooms and community gardens

Young Adults

Practical skills and a path to good work in a growing field.

  • Workforce training and job readiness
  • AI and technology in agriculture
  • Entrepreneur development
  • Climate-controlled, year-round growing skills

College Students

Real-world experience that builds résumés and careers.

  • Internships and hands-on training in aquaponics, AI, and sustainable agriculture
  • Partnerships with colleges and universities
  • Our hope: partner colleges will offer credit hours for students who take part
  • Research and innovation projects

The Whole Community

A welcoming place where neighbors learn, gather, and share.

  • Fresh, locally grown fish and produce, raised without chemical pesticides, plus family food production
  • Classes, events, and a community meeting hall
  • Fresh food baskets for food banks, shelters, and food-insecurity programs
  • ADA-compliant public areas, including parking, so everyone can take part
  • A model other communities can learn from

Programs shown are part of our planned vision and may grow and change as the project develops. College credit and partnerships depend on agreements with each school.

From Our Farm to Your Table

Our plan is to process and package our own fish and produce for sale on site, and to deliver fresh fish, greens, herbs, fruits, and vegetables to communities within about 50 miles of Okmulgee, such as Tulsa, Beggs, and Muskogee, using our AnchorPoints delivery truck. We also plan to process and bottle our own fish fertilizer for sale on site, and to offer online ordering and shipping.

All sales, delivery, and shipping plans will be finalized as the farm develops, and will follow the licenses and permits required.
